guide.title: Schubert: "Death and the Maiden" – III. Scherzo (Allegro molto)
guide.overview: This is a fast movement in 3/4 time. It has two big parts: a loud Part 1 that starts in D minor, and a much softer Trio that starts in D major. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so treat them as a guide. Listen for the jumps between loud and soft, and between minor (darker) and major (brighter).

listening_points.headline: A loud opening in D minor
listening_points.text: The first violin leads from the very first bar [m. 0-4]. The music starts loud, in D minor. The opening bar is in unison or octaves, meaning the players share the same notes.

listening_points.headline: Swell, then a sudden hush
listening_points.text: A crescendo (getting gradually louder) is marked in [m. 6]. Then the music drops suddenly to soft at [m. 8]. The key brightens to D major at [m. 9]. The second violin probably leads there.

listening_points.headline: Back to loud, in A minor
listening_points.text: The key moves to A minor at [m. 14]. The music is still soft. At [m. 17] it jumps to loud, with the players in unison or octaves.

listening_points.headline: The viola and second violin step forward
listening_points.text: Around [m. 22-23] the viola probably takes the lead. After that, the second violin probably leads in [m. 24-30]. The key shifts to G minor at [m. 26].

listening_points.headline: D minor, then A major, then a soft moment
listening_points.text: D minor comes back at [m. 29]. A major follows at [m. 31]. At [m. 32] the music suddenly turns soft. D minor returns at [m. 35].

listening_points.headline: Suddenly loud again in D minor
listening_points.text: At [m. 37] the music is suddenly loud again. The players are in unison or octaves. The key is D minor, and the first violin probably leads from [m. 41].

listening_points.headline: A brighter B-flat major patch
listening_points.text: The key turns to B-flat major at [m. 46]. It is loud at first. At [m. 49] it drops suddenly to soft.

listening_points.headline: Soft, then a build-up
listening_points.text: D minor returns at [m. 51], and a crescendo is marked. The music is soft in [m. 52-60]. B-flat major comes back at [m. 57]. Another crescendo is marked at [m. 61]. D minor returns at [m. 62].

listening_points.headline: The estimated loudest point
listening_points.text: A computer estimate marks [m. 63] as the loudest and busiest point. It is very loud, in D minor. The section ends in D major in [m. 65-67], still very loud.

listening_points.headline: The Trio begins, very soft
listening_points.text: The Trio starts with a single bar for the first violin alone [m. 68]. It is very soft. The key is A major from [m. 69], and the first violin leads over the others.

listening_points.headline: Short key shifts in the Trio
listening_points.text: The key moves to D major at [m. 78], then to G major at [m. 80]. The parts move together in chords there. D major returns at [m. 83]. At [m. 84] the music is suddenly a little louder, at soft.

listening_points.headline: Back to very soft, with a lone violin
listening_points.text: At [m. 101] the music drops suddenly to very soft. A crescendo is marked at [m. 106]. A diminuendo (getting gradually softer) is marked in [m. 107]. The first violin plays alone at [m. 108].

listening_points.headline: A darker turn to D minor
listening_points.text: The key darkens to D minor at [m. 111]. A crescendo is marked at [m. 113] and a diminuendo at [m. 114]. A major returns at [m. 117].

listening_points.headline: Gentle swells in D major and A major
listening_points.text: The key is D major in [m. 122-129], then A major from [m. 130]. The music gets a little louder, to soft, at [m. 132]. A crescendo is marked at [m. 137]. It returns to very soft at [m. 140].

listening_points.headline: A quiet ending in A major
listening_points.text: D minor appears in [m. 143-148]. D major follows at [m. 153]. A brief E major comes at [m. 159]. A diminuendo is marked at [m. 161]. The music ends very softly, in A major.

glossary.explanation: The name in this movement's title. Here the music is fast and has three beats to the bar (3/4).
The home note and scale that the music centres on. Minor sounds darker. Major sounds brighter.
The players play the same notes, or the same notes at different heights.
The parts move together in chords.
